on_your_files.fades_gated: Answer to your question (does 'below the open at entry' matter in our bigger sample): yes for the stock, not enough for the option. Clean equity-offering events, entered at the 09:31 close only when the stock was already below its open: last 3 months 6 events, the stock fell further in 6 of 6, average -1.4% to the close (-1.0% without the best, -0.7% without the best two); the 0.25-delta put with our live exit still -21% / -37% / -51%. Two years, 14 gated events: stock -1.0% average (0.0% without the best), put +2% / -16% / -25%. Ungated 10:00 entries are worse (3 months 12 events, 4 fell, put -39% / -45%). So position gating turns a coin flip into a small drift, and a small drift does not pay for a weekly put. Your CRWV (chased after the gap) vs MRVL (in-session headline, +500%) fits: the in-session arrival is the edge, not the position. Full tables: journal/research/FADES.md on our main
